comparisons.peer_topic: Revolving Credit Facility Limits and Maturities
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, the company expanded its 5-year $5.0 billion and 364-day $5.0 billion revolving credit facilities to $7.0 billion and $8.0 billion respectively, with maturity dates extended to February 2029 and January 2025. These facilities are unsecured general obligations and had no borrowings outstanding as of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and INTC disclosed the status of their unsecured credit facilities in Item 8. AVGO’s 2023 Term Loans were specifically unsecured facilities totaling $30.39 billion entered into in connection with the VMware Merger. INTC also disclosed that its expanded revolving credit facilities (aggregating up to $15 billion) are 'unsecured general obligations' with no outstanding borrowings as of the end of 2024. While AVGO disclosed active term loan borrowings, INTC disclosed no outstanding borrowings under its unsecured facilities, highlighting a difference in leverage usage despite both maintaining unsecured facility structures.

sentences.text: Upon completion of the VMware Merger, we entered an $11,195 million unsecured term A-2 facility (the "Term A-2 Loan"), an $11,195 million unsecured term A-3 facility (the "Term A-3 Loan"), and an $8,000 million unsecured term A-5 facility (the "Term A-5 Loan", collectively, the "2023 Term Loans").
These credit facilities are unsecured general obligations.
The revolving credit facilities had no borrowings outstanding as of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023.

comparisons.peer_summary: In 2023, the company issued $6.70 billion of senior unsecured notes and term loans, receiving $6.69 billion in cash, and prepaid $600 million of the 2024 Term Loan A principal.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU disclosed significant term loan issuances related to corporate financing activities in 2023/2024. AVGO entered into three unsecured term loan facilities totaling $30,390 million in connection with the VMware Merger. MU issued $6.70 billion of senior unsecured notes and term loan agreements in 2023, receiving $6.69 billion in cash. Both companies utilized unsecured term loans as a primary instrument for raising capital, although AVGO’s borrowing was explicitly tied to a merger consideration while MU’s was part of a broader debt issuance strategy.
